app/src/views.js:373-396 — abilityPage is a self-contained function
app/src/views.js:257-266 — but the Abilities section is embedded inside pokemonPage
app/src/views.js:62 — and the 'hidden' flag leaks into the shared pokemonCard component

removability.rationale: Routes and view functions are colocated per feature and everything is greppable, but removal touches three files, and the card flag and CSS rule are scattered remnants rather than a single deletable unit.

evidence: app/src/views.js:227-231 — inline reimplementation of latestEnglishFlavor that already exists at app/src/api.js:46-50
app/src/api.js:42-43 — englishGenus is dead code; views.js:226 inlines its own genus lookup
app/src/views.js:186 — typeEn lambda duplicated at app.js:112, views.js:349, views.js:379, views.js:426
app/src/views.js:65 — sprite URL rule is centralized in one card component (good)
changeability.rationale: The card/sprite fixes genuinely land in one place thanks to the single pokemonCard component, but shared formatting rules (flavor text, genus, type names) each live in two or five places, so a rule change is an N-place fix.

evidence: app/src/views.js:151 — index.typeEn.get.bind(index.typeEn) passed into cardGrid; views consume index internals
app/public/app.js:2-9 — client tweak couples to the 'omit empty params' URL convention also implemented server-side at views.js:138-146
app/src/app.js:63,158 — HX-Request branching keeps full-page vs fragment rendering in one route each (clean seam)
coupling.rationale: Module roles are clean and server/client separation is excellent (11 lines of client JS), but views depend on the raw shape of the index object and the typeEn helper is threaded through every component rather than exposed once.

evidence: app/src/views.js:78-80 — cardGrid/pokemonCard stretch across four list contexts with only two justified flags (showTypes, hidden)
app/src/views.js:133,315 — homeResults doubles as page and htmx fragment; movesTable doubles as initial render and sort target
app/src/views.js:387-392 — abilityPage bypasses cardGrid and hand-rolls the card list, breaking the single abstraction
app/src/views.js:344-371,373-396 — movePage/abilityPage share an h1+Effect pattern with no resource-page abstraction; an Items page copies it
abstraction_design.rationale: The core abstractions (card, section, moves table, dual-render fragment) are designed around the app's real variation and reused rather than copied; the residue is small — a bypassed cardGrid and near-duplicate page skeletons.

findings.issue: The 'latest English flavor text, whitespace collapsed' rule is implemented twice: latestEnglishFlavor (api.js:46) for moves, an inline copy in pokemonPage.
findings.suggestion: Have pokemonPage import and call latestEnglishFlavor; delete the inline version.

findings.issue: The typeEn fallback lambda is duplicated five times (app.js:112, views.js:186, 349, 379, 426) and passed as a component option, including via index.typeEn.get.bind (views.js:151).
findings.suggestion: Export one typeEn(name) helper from api.js (or attach it to the index object) and use it everywhere.

findings.issue: abilityPage hand-rolls <ul class="cards"> around pokemonCard instead of using cardGrid, creating a second render path for card lists (a sort-in-cardGrid change would miss this list).
findings.suggestion: Extend cardGrid with the hidden flag (e.g. per-item options) and use it in abilityPage.

findings.issue: englishGenus is dead code while pokemonPage re-implements the genus lookup inline (views.js:226).
findings.suggestion: Either use englishGenus in pokemonPage or delete it.

findings.issue: Views reach into the index object's internals (typeEn Map, types, generations) — the index shape is an implicit contract shared by api.js, app.js and views.js.
findings.suggestion: Return ready-to-use display values (or accessor helpers) from getIndex so views never touch Map internals.

findings.issue: Media URL knowledge is concentrated in spriteUrl/artworkUrl but pokemonPage also hardcodes an artwork fallback by pattern (views.js:241).
findings.suggestion: Move the fallback decision into api.js (e.g. artworkFor(pokemon)) so views never construct media URLs.

findings.issue: The 'omit empty/default query params' convention is implemented twice: client-side in the htmx:configRequest tweak and server-side in pageUrl (views.js:138-146).
findings.suggestion: Document the coupling next to both, or build URLs in one place and pass them.

findings.issue: serveStatic uses cwd-relative paths ('./public/...'); starting the server from another directory silently breaks assets.
findings.suggestion: Resolve paths against import.meta.url (new URL('../public/...', import.meta.url).pathname).

findings.issue: Cache is unbounded, has no TTL, and caches nulls for 404s; changing caching rules means reworking the promise-cache pattern, though it is at least confined to one file.
findings.suggestion: Wrap responses (value + timestamp) instead of promises to make TTL/invalidation a drop-in change.

findings.issue: Moves-table sorting lives in app.js (SORT_KEYS, sortedRows) while its rendering contract (sort/dir strings) lives in movesTable (views.js:313-337); adding a column means editing both plus the /moves-table endpoint's query parsing.
findings.suggestion: Move SORT_KEYS next to the row-shape construction in buildMovesData so column and sort key are defined together.

summary: A small, clearly-factored app — one data module, colocated routes and view functions, and a single card component that makes most card changes one-place fixes. The main editability drag is shallow duplication: the flavor-text rule, genus lookup, and typeEn helper each exist in two or five copies, and abilityPage bypasses the cardGrid abstraction. Data-source and caching knowledge is exemplary, confined to one file; the index's species objects lack Pokémon-level data, which is the one place a 'wrong sprite' fix would need real plumbing.

scenarios.change: Remove the Abilities pages and every link to them
scenarios.notes: Route and view function are contiguous blocks, but the Abilities section inside pokemonPage, the 'hidden' flag on the shared card, and the CSS rule are scattered remnants across three files.

scenarios.change: Fix wrong sprite for species whose default Pokémon has a different name (e.g. Deoxys)
scenarios.notes: One fix does cover every list — all cards render via pokemonCard and spriteUrl is a single helper. But the index's species objects carry no Pokémon data, so a data-driven fix means extending buildIndex (per-species fetches) and threading the new field, not just editing the card.

scenarios.change: Add sorting by name to every list of Pokémon cards
scenarios.notes: cardGrid is the choke point and one sort covers home, move and type lists — but abilityPage bypasses cardGrid (views.js:387-392), so the fourth list needs a separate edit or it silently stays unsorted.

scenarios.change: Add an Items section (/items, /items/:name) shaped like Moves
scenarios.notes: Layout, section, apiFetch, humanize/englishName and typeBadgeLink are directly reusable; the movePage body and typesPage list have no generic resource-page abstraction, so the page bodies are copied, and getIndex needs an items extension. Roughly half reused, half copied.

scenarios.change: Change the API base URL and caching rules
scenarios.notes: Only one file knows anything: base URL, cache, media URL patterns and index build are all in api.js. But that's four distinct spots in the file, and the promise-based cache would need rework for TTL/invalidation.
